research_question: When can a ranking predict allocation?
stage_i_anchor: CT2 ordinal insufficiency; CT3 forced reversal
stage_i_status: Boundary proved; positive rank-preservation conditions absent
stage_ii_target: Define the allocation identified set over admissible cardinalizations, feasible sets and selection rules; prove sufficient restricted conditions for rank preservation or set collapse
simulation_requirement: Construct rank-equivalent score transformations and controlled feasible-set cases; recover the proved boundary and positive cases
empirical_requirement: Test whether pre-decision score order and acreage-share order co-move under explicitly observable conditions without claiming optimality
acceptance_gate: All objects and assumptions are explicit; theorem proof is complete; counterexamples show each dropped assumption matters

research_question: How do cardinal profit margins alter allocation?
stage_ii_target: Formalize a margin channel that distinguishes ordinal rank from cardinal distance and states its interaction with selection and constraints
simulation_requirement: M0 ranking to M1 expected-profit experiment varies only margin scale/gap with common scenarios
empirical_requirement: Build geography-time-aligned pre-decision margin ranks and continuous margin gaps
acceptance_gate: No units mismatch; fixed-rank transformations and cardinal gaps have separate claims

research_question: Which local optimality pressures support a reversal?
stage_i_status: Complete stationarity but no quantitative scientific decomposition
stage_ii_target: Define margin, tail-risk, budget, shared-constraint and bound pressure terms with signs and units; label them local optimality pressures
simulation_requirement: Report every term and residual at controlled solutions; no omitted multiplier
empirical_requirement: Only mechanisms with observed inputs may receive an empirical analogue
acceptance_gate: Terms exactly reconstruct stationarity within tolerance; text never calls them additive acreage causes
manuscript_destination: Stochastic optimization model; Ranking reversal mechanisms

research_question: How can acreage changes be attributed across model blocks?
stage_ii_target: Define nested counterfactual attribution M0--M4 with a declared deterministic selection and optimal-face attribution intervals; document order dependence or use a justified symmetric rule
simulation_requirement: Compute block additions and permutation/order sensitivity for acreage, profit and CVaR
empirical_requirement: Do not transfer simulation attribution labels to observed acreage without identified inputs
acceptance_gate: Attribution sums to the total selected-model change; face and order uncertainty are reported

research_question: When do operational constraints force or reshape reversal?
stage_i_status: Extreme sufficient result proved; general quantitative effect absent
stage_ii_target: Classify direct forcing, marginal pressure and boundary-selection effects for land, budget, rotation, contracts and bounds
simulation_requirement: One-at-a-time tightness sweeps plus interaction experiments; record slacks, duals, active sets and face ranges
empirical_requirement: Operational variables are tagged observed, proxy or unavailable; transitions may test inertia/rotation predictions
acceptance_gate: Each constraint has a proposition or explicit hypothesis and a falsification test

research_question: How does downside risk change allocation?
stage_i_status: Slack boundary proved; controlled binding effect absent
stage_ii_target: State the exact no-effect condition and conditional properties of the risk-feasible-set contraction; avoid crop-specific monotonicity without proof
simulation_requirement: M2 versus M3 comparisons vary alpha and kappa with all other inputs fixed; report allocation, expected profit, CVaR and risk dual
empirical_requirement: Aggregate data may test downside-exposure associations but cannot reveal a farmer CVaR limit
acceptance_gate: Slack cases show zero set/value effect as defined; binding cases are reported with nonmonotone/null outcomes retained

research_question: How does dependence affect downside risk and allocation?
stage_i_status: Correct restricted boundary; required order not established for the intended families
stage_ii_target: Prove any within-family loss-order result actually used; otherwise declare family-specific allocation response a numerical hypothesis
simulation_requirement: Fixed marginals, constraints and random streams; dense within-family dependence sweeps; cross-family results labelled sensitivity
empirical_requirement: Estimate dependence only from synchronized outcomes with uncertainty; no scalar coefficient is treated as causal
acceptance_gate: Every theorem names domain, family, marginals, order and optimizer assumptions

research_question: When do reversal regimes or crossing sets occur?
stage_i_status: Set logic proved; Stage I LHS crossings confounded
stage_ii_target: Specify continuity/selection assumptions for any point crossing; otherwise retain no, interval and multiple crossings as primary outcomes
simulation_requirement: Adaptive fixed-factor grids with active-basis/face tracking and independent replication
empirical_requirement: No empirical threshold claim without a pre-specified estimand and sufficient time support
acceptance_gate: Algorithm recovers synthetic known crossings and reports topology plus uncertainty

stage_ii_target: Separate variance diversification, tail diversification, allocation concentration, pseudo-diversification and true-law decision regret
simulation_requirement: Risk-return frontiers under true and misspecified dependence; leave-one-crop and marginal tail-contribution checks
empirical_requirement: Observed diversification claims require synchronized profit outcomes and cannot imply welfare without a decision model
acceptance_gate: Each construct has a unit, comparator, direction and non-equivalence counterexample

research_question: When does information create value under flexibility?
stage_i_anchor: CT10 actionability and weak flexibility monotonicity
stage_i_status: General safe result proved; strict complementarity absent
stage_ii_target: Give sufficient increasing-differences/lattice or problem-specific conditions for complementarity; otherwise pre-register an interaction hypothesis and substitution counterexamples
simulation_requirement: Fully crossed signal precision by nested action-set design; report policies, VOI, interaction contrasts and zero/substitute cases
empirical_requirement: Use timestamped pre-decision information and observable flexibility only; causal language requires exogenous variation
acceptance_gate: Decision timing is coherent; ignore-signal policy feasible; complementarity and substitution outcomes are both allowed

research_question: Which model predictions are empirically observable?
stage_i_status: Ten constructs mapped but most mechanisms partly observed or unavailable
stage_ii_target: Replace binary link language with prediction, observable, proxy, sign, timing, aggregation and identification fields
simulation_requirement: Generate simulation estimands on the same scale as proposed empirical outcomes
empirical_requirement: Pre-register transition, heterogeneity, temporal and aggregation tests with explicit non-identification boundaries
acceptance_gate: Every empirical claim names the model prediction and its observable status

research_question: Which historical proof gaps remain research gaps?
stage_i_status: 18 Draft gaps say OPEN_FOR_REPAIR although canonical transitions repair, replace or reject them
stage_ii_target: Create a reconciled registry distinguishing CLOSED_BY_REPAIR, CLOSED_BY_REPLACEMENT, FALSE_BOUNDARY_RETAINED and OPEN_STAGE_II
simulation_requirement: Validators require every Draft gap to map to a canonical result or an explicit open Stage II target
acceptance_gate: No gap is silently deleted; no repaired Draft claim is reintroduced under a new label
